Median minimum in-grip clearance 66 mm, median held time 2.845 s, and upward body motion at 0.30 s falls to median 6 mm. On this smaller carry subset, none reach support before losing contact and nine leave the zone first. Lowering improved proximal height and time while losing critical early funnel stages and producing violations. No checkpoint is retained. All four L40S profiled for 90 updates. Measured active rate 108,397 steps/s including startup, 110,256 after two updates. Median per-device times 7.279 s physics, 1.738 s control, 0.700 s sensor, 0.139 s inference, 1.905 s resets, 1.836 s optimizer including 0.367 s sync. No capacity overflow and 35 completed exact contract samples without problems. The matched noise intervention r0134 is running. The previous high-noise checkpoint remains the incumbent.

body.text: The active sigma 0.35 experiment changes the optimiser regime. At update 15 each of the four ranks collected about 490k active samples but processed only two local 4096-sample minibatches before the PPO KL guard, giving 1.7 percent of a first epoch. Updates 3–16 mostly show this behaviour with early logged mean KL about 0.026–0.093 (target .023); the 2.226 run normally spends about 1.8 s optimizing compared with ~0.011 s here. First training completions are 81/24576 vs seven with saturation, but are only 15-frame release milestones. On a synthetic PPO diagnostic using only copied weights, independent curriculum observations and fixed artificial value residuals, reducing Adam LR from 0.00028 to 0.000065 or 0.000044 increases tolerated minibatches from two to ten or fourteen and decreases direct Gaussian KL from 0.126 to 0.056 or 0.042. No probe weights are saved or reused. If the live comparison remains KL-limited and exact stages plateau, test 0.000044 from the same optimizer and actor with sigma 0.35, then compare minibatch use, attained exact task stages and measured throughput at all four GPUs. Result work/fixed_noise_learning_rate_probe.json.

body.text: Static signed distance of the middle and ring hulls at the actual [redacted] encoder configurations gives a directional check. In all 32 samples from 0 to 0.10 s across eight trials, the nearest bare hulls overlap, and their local separation increases if ring MCP2 decreases or middle MCP2 increases. That agrees with the operator report of a mechanical push toward negative ring angle. In the eight samples around 0.30–0.33 s where ring is already more than 0.02 rad under the limit, the nearest bare hulls have separated by 1.63–1.80 mm. This is consistent with using start-pose clearance to avoid the initial push and explains why an exact fit of excursion amplitude cannot be inferred from the bare overlap at the late encoder peak. It leaves real glove shape, contact history and actuator response uncertain. Evidence work/finger_contact/[redacted]_hull_sensitivity.json. Frozen gate unchanged.

body.text: Prospective carry-height reward validated on 128 matched Warp control rollouts. At 32 each, fixed-target hold and level transfer earn exactly zero new height credit. Level reaches the upright goal entry on 23, directed descent on 22. Descent reaches held upright support on 11 (zero level), receives median 0.909 height credit versus random 0.272, and triggers two arm stops. Random reaches zero entries and supports. Zero finger-travel violations and capacity errors across all 128. CPU results r0136/r0141 agree about direction and support. This is reward and physical-margin evidence only. The learning-rate comparison deliberately has the new carry-height option disabled. Files training/gpu/carry_height.py and work/carry_height_warp_probe.json.

The actual paired lower-LR run restores PPO batch use. With sigma 0.35 and the same start/seed/rollout settings, the first four .000044 updates use 7, 468, 480 and 480 minibatches per rank, with mean estimated KL .0192, .00774, .01324 and .01424. The old .00028 comparison uses two on its corresponding early updates, with early mean KL .0244, .0272, .0382 and .0737. Rollout samples through initial ramp and restarts remain close (6.687M vs 6.691M at update four). More effective optimization adds about 1.8–2.3 s per warm update, as expected. These are optimization diagnostics only; hold exact policy judgments until the fixed 64 trials. Evidence work/ppo_gpu_10_lower_lr/curves.csv and profile_00001 through profile_00004.

body.text: The fresh carry gate r0161 rejected r0158. Counts 32 lifts, 20 turns, 19 carries, zero placements, stops and violations. The incumbent matched 32/22/16 with no faults. Keep r0106 as the deployment incumbent and use the same r0106 weights/moments and -.100 pose as both earlier optimizer comparisons for the isolated next reward test. Test only optional weighted upright carry-height shaping r0157 over low-noise/lower-rate baseline, if its queued Warp controls pass. The objective is supported seat then placement, not another fragile isolated carry gain. No target submission for r0158. r0159 gives zero faults on 16 contact-enabled delayed diagnostics for reference.

Matched Warp revalidation of weighted carry height r0157 has 32 controls per mode. Fixed hold pays zero for total carry, level gives 4.733, directed descend gives 7.455, random 0.539. Additional causal height credit median 0.892 descend, 0.317 random, exactly zero in holds/level. Descending produces 22 upright entries and 11 supported seats, with two table-clearance stops. Level 23 entries and zero support. Random zero entries/support and one travel excursion. No capacity errors. body.text: Prepare a training-only carry completion variant for a later isolated test if R12 plateaus. The demonstrated adapted body centre is about 20 mm above standing at goal entry. The weighted reward modifies height by roughly 6–13 mm but every ordered carry still enters around 115–126 mm above support and loses the grip in air. In the matched 53-state physical test, 51 directed descents enter upright and reach within 35 mm of standing while held, versus two level transfers, and 24 reach support. Delay the carry bonus and entry to the seating phase until the plug is upright and transferred while held within 35 mm of standing. Require uninterrupted unsupported contact and measured/commanded palm motion for a newly acquired low posture. An already-low held starting grip remains eligible if it stays controlled. Exact gate and deployment criteria are unchanged. Six tensor control cases pass, including rejecting passive lowering and foregone contact. Before using, run the 128 exact Warp controls with the new gate using work/check_warp_carry_height.py --low-handoff. It is disabled in currently training R12.

reward_terms.name: approach
reward_terms.formula: New maximum of approach potential from housing-to-palm position, wrist angle and two intended pads near the housing.

reward_terms.name: lift
reward_terms.formula: New clearance potential of a gripped object, gated by opposed contact and referenced to 14 mm.

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: New maximum of the minimum of world blade-up progress and signed tilt reduction attributable to relative angle changes; paid only while continuously opposed, unsupported, and the contact digits have measured and commanded motion. Common wrist rotation cancels in the relative measurement.

reward_terms.name: carry
reward_terms.formula: Planar progress with weight 9 is multiplied by 0.25 + 0.75 times the measured height quality. Up to 6 points of causal height progress are added. The height target interpolates the reconstructed transfer at the current lateral position, with 10 mm tolerance and 100 mm Gaussian scale. The upright plug remains held and unsupported through all controller ticks, the palm moves at least half as far as the object in the same vertical direction and its target changes in that direction. Only a new height-quality maximum pays.

reward_terms.name: seat
reward_terms.formula: New combined seating potential. Height score uses a 2 mm tolerance and 100 mm scale. Height credit requires an actual decrease in height error with downward movement at the palm of at least half of that distance, a descending target, blades within 25 degrees and contact preserved across controller ticks. Both policy samples are inside the goal. Tilt guidance keeps its existing scale. The potential starts at the measured entry value.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: New gain in removal of hand contact and supported upright rest.

reward_terms.name: reference_object

reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in five-digit demonstrated flexion agreement with 0.53 rad RMS tolerance.

reward_terms.name: reference_contact
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in object-frame contact agreement with reconstructed witnesses within a 9 mm free band.

reward_terms.name: bonus
reward_terms.formula: One-time ordered approach, lift, turn, carry, seat and release bonuses 4, 6, 10, 12, 14 and 30.

reward_terms.name: slip
reward_terms.formula: Negative blade-angle displacement past 0.10 degree when an opposed grip moves the object with nearly stationary finger joints.

reward_terms.name: regularity
reward_terms.formula: Negative mean absolute target change, metres and radians.

reward_terms.name: stop
reward_terms.formula: Penalty at station stop or hardware violation.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Penalty on a dropped plug that settles unturned during the supported manipulation.

The exact CPU PoseSensor initializes empty on all 53 saved actual mid-transfer states and all 23 high preseat states because the plug is already occluded, with median initial position errors 544 and 521 mm, invalid flag and age zero. Travel faults one cold and zero with stale cache. This is a diagnostic of reset-observation mismatch and is not an observation change on the deployed policy. Check actual Warp reset for the recorded state poses and export the original invalid-but-cached v3 poses and ages for a possible isolated guided-cache study. Evidence work/curriculum_sensor_reset_mismatch.json and work/mid_carry_reset_sensor_comparison.json. GPU check is queued after training so profiling stays isolated.

body.text: At-goal causal intervention on 24 exact r0158 carriers, replaying the actual deployment prefix and branching at the next policy tick after first upright held entry. Original targets hold another median .505 s. Holding only fingers gives .745 s, holding only the commanded palm .495, holding both 1.630. `None` of those contacts reach support. Holding the same finger targets while braking in the footprint and lowering the palm gives median 1.130 s, contact through support in nine and upright held support in eight, all from actual high entries. All 120 runs zero hardware faults and stops. This demonstrates that both continued arm motion and further finger targets can contribute to grip loss and that controlled descent from the actual high grip is sometimes physically possible. It is a diagnostic counterfactual, not training data. Evidence work/r0158_goal_grip_intervention.json.

body.reflection: Controlled 35 mm carry-to-seat handoff at 35,596,587 new active steps. The fixed64 exact deployment check finds 64 lifts, 38 turns, 20 carries, no qualifying place or success, zero hardware violations or stops, 12 rests and act() p99 0.264 ms. Matched R12 C1 gives 64/39/29, no travel violation and one late arm table stop. Median entry and minimum still-held clearance 133/109 mm versus 124/119, and median holding duration 0.785 versus 0.410 s. All 20 release before support and 15 first exit the goal. Median object initially rises 32 mm. The first sampled full horizon produced no training completion at the more demanding handoff, as expected for the initially high path. This is a proximal grip-duration change and no exact placement improvement. r0185 separately finds eight physically supported seats by braking and lowering once the r0158 plug has already reached the zone in actual high grasps. `None` of those scripted commands enter training.

body.text: Prepared a staged physical preseat reset distribution for later, with sensor history. From the independent 96-start r0158 collection, replay the 41 verified upright carries through their actual entry, then make the same diagnostic brake and descent validated in r0185. 20 of 41 reach upright support while still held, no faults/stops. Sample 117 physical joint/object states at heights 27, 47, 67, 87, 107 and 127 mm above standing from those successful descent trajectories. In actual exact physics restore, 99 states hold continuous opposition, clear of support and in goal for .20 s in both nominal and .1075 s/.010 rad brackets. Bin counts 20/20/20/19/15/5 across 20 source seeds, all have real invalid camera caches measured during replay. Append only those 99 phase-4 snapshots to the 292-state bank, total 391. No action sequences, motion targets as training labels, teacher loss or changes to deployment input. Files work/training_reset_pool_seat_bridge.json, work/seat_bridge_sensor_cache.json and work/preseat_bridge_diagnostic.json. Compare existing actors from these levels before adopting a new training curriculum.

body.text: Exploration diagnosis on exact contract observations. Around first upright goal entry the r0158, r0186 and r0188 actors produce positive wrist-Z latent means on 84–85 percent of sampled held observations, medians .564, .566 and .499. Under latent sigma .35, median marginal probability of a negative Z latent on those fixed observations is .053, .053 and .077. On the 99 preseat snapshots, the same r0188 mean has cold-cache median .714 (marginal .021) and real recorded stale-cache median 3.572 (marginal 9.2e-25). Fixed-observation marginals do not predict closed-loop trajectories. A paired r0186 test from all 99 passes zero held seat advances cold and with actual stale cache; travel faults are nine cold, zero restored. The actual cache is a genuine deployment input and can accentuate an initially rising action, so warming alone is not a placement result. Evaluate short fixed-bias diagnostic counterfactuals before considering temporally correlated vertical exploration, separate from the physically staged reset curriculum. Evidence work/r0158_vertical_exploration.json, work/low_handoff_c2_vertical_exploration.json, work/preseat_bridge_policy_probe.json.

body.reflection: Controlled 35 mm low transition after 108,268,028 new interactions. Exact fixed64 counts 64 lifts, 42 turns, 27 carries, zero qualifying places or successes, zero faults and stops, 14 rests and act() p99 .270 ms. Matched R12 gives 64/37/34 with zero faults. Median goal entry 122 mm, median minimum while held 102 mm, 0.680 s hold. Compared to matched 127/121 mm and .345 s, carry retention improves on its own subset, but all 27 still detach airborne and 19 first leave the zone. Median early upward motion remains 20 mm. It has yet to meet the task's placement. r0187 fills a measured near-support curriculum gap, and r0189 indicates that independent .35 latent noise seldom samples downward around the actual handoff output. Both lines of work are being tested separately from this ongoing reward change.

body.text: Diagnostic persistent downward offsets are insufficient by themselves. On all 99 validated preseat starts with r0186, 24-step vertical-only offsets of -.8, -1.6 and -3.5 produce 0, 1 and 4 supported-seat advances with actual recorded caches and 0, 1 and 2 settled releases. With cold caches they produce 1, 4 and 44 advances but 47, 71 and 70 stops, and no resulting settlements. Warm has no stops and zero, zero and two measured travel faults respectively. These are controller counterfactuals, not policy changes. The duration-limited tests completed for all cases; two longer constant-offset diagnostics ended without results. The sign and steadiness of vertical motion matter, with grip and planarity still limiting the outcome. Preserve validated physical state coverage first. Temporal exploration remains a possible later PPO setting, with exact stop termination. Evidence work/preseat_short_vertical_bias_*.json.

The low handoff run R13 helps preserve grip, but its 144.09M checkpoint still loses contact before support on all 35 ordered carries in 64 exact starts. In the sampled training log through 170.73M, 38 of 121,322 completed full-start episodes reach the low handoff and none remain completely settled at the horizon by the training proxy. The preceding matched study without the low rule had 265 full-start proxy completions and zero exact completions. r0161 shows the same separation before support in seeds 1024693583 and 1570065137. Next matched 26-minute study keeps the low handoff and existing PPO settings and adds only r0187’s physical preseat reset bank at 27–127 mm, after checking restoration in Warp. It retains cold sensor reset behavior to isolate start geometry. I expect more phase-4 training progress, lower held clearance on the same 64 exact starts, and held support before separation. body.reflection: The 176.43M endpoint of the low carry handoff study had 64 lifts, 34 active turns, 21 ordered carries, zero ordered placements, zero faults and stops and 11 terminal rests. Conditioned on those 21 carries, median entry and minimum still-held clearances were 119 and 98 mm, with 0.740 s remaining hold. At 0.30 s past entry, or earlier separation, median target rise was 56 mm. All 21 detached before support, 18 after leaving the footprint. One later held seat occurred after the original contact had already been broken. The matched 178.10M run without the lower handoff had 31 carries at 121/111 mm and 0.56 s, zero placement, one arm travel fault and zero stops. The stricter handoff made a longer low grip more common but it yielded no exact placements. No checkpoint retained. All four GPUs averaged 112,156 active env steps/s including startup and 114,128 after two warm-up updates. Median per-rank physics 7.088 s, controller 1.739 s, sensor .695 s, inference .137 s, resets 1.463 s, PPO 1.839 s including .370 s collectives. Zero capacity overflows and zero problems in 34 completed exact contract audit streams. The next study r0192/r0194 tests additional physically validated preseat resets.

body.text: The current carry height bonus has almost no headroom at the start of full carries. On the 35 exact r0193 carries, at the first opposed upright grip in the continuous carried interval, median alignment with the retargeted height curve was .997. At first upright goal entry it was .441. The median reconstructed maximum-better height credit is zero, and all 35 detach before support. The height-weighted planar reward can still favor going high quickly. A prospective training-only charge for new accumulated height deviation in continuous upright transfer would make excessive ascent visible to the reward without paying repeated reductions. At weight 4 its replayed median charge would be -3.93 within the observed held transfer. Evidence work/r0193_carry_height_credit.json. I will compare matched physical holding, level, ascent, descent and random controls before any such run. R14 continues with its existing reward.

body.text: On 24 nominal exact starts chosen from the r0158 collection, replayed the original commands through the first 100 Hz frame that satisfies the frozen in-hand turn criterion. The continuation from that prefix is a diagnostic controller only. Original continuation gave 20 upright goal entries at median 137 mm above standing and zero held support. Replaying fixed fingers with a slower level transfer gave 23 entries at 54 mm and zero held support. Starting the reconstructed low transfer immediately after the verified turn with the same fixed grip gave 22 entries at 19 mm and 24 in-zone first support contacts while still held. Four already met the upright seated geometry at first support. All 72 controls were free of stops and travel violations. The exact original prefix is sufficient for a low transfer that retains the grip. Seating orientation remains variable. Evidence work/low_transfer_exact_probe.json. No action from the diagnostic is a training label or part of deployment.

On 25 of 31 prepared phase-5 states that restored with both hand contact and table support, all or most actors achieved a half-second stable release during their exact-station 30-second suffix. For the same-start parent, R13 C4 and R14 C1 the counts were 25/22/25 initially, 7/9/7 with stable upright release at the final half-second and 3/4/2 satisfying both terminal release and measured robot rest without violations. Both the return and the end of the trial matter. Cold pose estimates were initially invalid in all 25. These prepared suffixes are diagnostic, separate from full-start criteria and gate counts. Evidence work/seat_release_matched_probe.json. A later study can align the release shaping with measured half-second robot rest once ordered seating is reached.

The same 24 exact r0198 prefixes and low transfer 19 mm entry geometry also support a small physical wrist alignment intervention after the verified in-hand turn. Adjusting the wrist toward blade-up around the measured carried body, with the same fixed grip and planned object path, preserves 24/24 in-zone held first support contacts and improves qualifying upright first seats from 4/24 to 14/24. Median tilt at support falls from 15.7 to 8.0 degrees. No stops or hardware excursions across all 48 runs. The first unsupported upright goal entry remains comparable at median 18.9 versus 18.6 mm. This uses measured simulated pose at the cut for a diagnostic only. It gives a source of physically viable low-carry snapshots if added early-carry training coverage is needed. Evidence work/low_transfer_alignment_exact.json.

body.text: R15 tests the isolated height-deviation charge r0196 after the R14 expanded reset study, which still had zero ordered placements through 144.09M. The latest official freeze r0161 shows early contact then flat, disconnected plugs in seeds 1024693583 and 1570065137. On 160 paired Warp controls, median added charge on fixed/level/descending/random/ascending motions is -.005/-.581/-.001/-.496/-1.893, with no positive added reward. The descending group has 20 low handoffs, 11 upright held seats and two table clearance stops; other groups have no low handoffs. One random travel fault, zero contact or solver capacity errors. Evidence work/carry_height_deviation_warp.json. R15 keeps the R14 parent weights and Adam, seed, 388-state bank, cold sensor, fixed .35 exploration, learning rate .000044, -.100 rad middle MCP2, 26 min, physical sim4 strata and exact CPU evaluator. Only the new-magnitude penalty, capped at 4 per carry phase, is switched on. Expect less rise within 0.30 s after a verified turn and lower held goal entries before more supported seating. R14 endpoint exact evidence is processing. The separate low transfer bank is not used.

All 34 low phase-3 states from r0202 also survived the six stepped Warp restoration test with unsupported opposed grip, blade tilt at most 25 degrees and clearance at least 10 mm. 21 measured rows each, zero travel faults, no geometric stop, no capacity departure. Low-band height range 18.2–54.5 mm above standing. Evidence work/low_transfer_midway_warp.json. Candidate curriculum for a later matched phase-3 coverage study, separate from the current deviation charge.

body.reflection: The 178.13M endpoint with the 388-state bank had 64 lifts, 47 active turns, 29 held upright carries, zero ordered placements or successes, zero travel violations, one arm clearance stop and 12 final rests. Seed 1017810 stopped at 18.34 s, 8.85 mm commanded table clearance. Compared with R13 endpoint 64/34/21, the enlarged preseat bank yielded more turns and carries, together with the one later stop. For this endpoint median entry/minimum still-held clearance was 125/116 mm and grip .570 s versus 119/98 mm and .740 s from the smaller bank. All 29 release before support and 26 first leave the footprint. The upper targets still rise a median 67 mm in the first .30 s from entry. No trained candidate retained from the run. The total actual throughput was 114,087 active env steps/s inclusive and 116,168 after two updates, with four L40S. Median physics 7.026 s, controller 1.738 s, sensor .713 s, inference .141 s, resets 1.406 s and PPO 1.876 s including .372 s synchronization. No capacity overflow and no problems in any of the 35 complete sampled exact contract audit streams. R15 isolates the height-deviation penalty tested in r0206.

body.text: The r0208 network was replayed for a full 30 s from each of 34 physically validated low phase-3 snapshots under identical nominal dynamics and matched observation RNG. The cold-cache condition enters the goal upright and held within 35 mm on 22/34, reaches six supported upright seats there in the original continuous grip, with two travel violations and one stop. The actual recorded retained pose condition reaches that low opening on 1/34, has zero consecutive seats, stops or excursions. There is zero complete suffix either way. The added low states therefore offer a learning route, and the stale-state distribution connects the training opportunity to the end-to-end sensor failure. The prepared suffix is diagnostic. Evidence work/r14_endpoint_low_transfer_cold.json and work/r14_endpoint_low_transfer_recorded.json. These states and caches remain inactive in R15.

Two diagnostics inform the next exploration choice. On the 34 low restores from r0209, initial mean vertical latent median is -.055 for cold and +2.226 with the actual retained cache. Removing the age feature alone leaves +2.094; removing only retained position and orientation while keeping real age shifts it to -.341. This isolates the stale pose values as the dominant association at those observations. Separately, on 48 paired six-second full starts, independent .35 exploration and the same noise plus a zero-mean .90 vertical offset resampled every 24 eligible steps both give 48 lifts, 35 turns, zero held low entries, zero seats and zero stops or violations. Ordered carry is 21 versus 24. The offset is active only in the camera-lost late workspace based on observations. Median rise over the first .30 s from verified turn is 67.1 versus 64.7 mm. No training or deployment change from either probe. Files work/low_transfer_cache_feature_ablation.json and work/coherent_vertical_noise_exact/summary.json; the coherent sampling diagnostic is motivated by periodic exploration in https://proceedings.mlr.press/v164/raffin22a.html.

The actual station sensor and command limiter remain exact. This is only a fixed-weight observation diagnostic. At the 34 matched reset snapshots, clearing position alone gives median vertical latent .994, clearing orientation alone .392, both -.341, versus 2.226 with actual stale values. Evidence work/stale_pose_mask_exact/summary.json and work/low_transfer_cache_pose_component_ablation.json. Next paired diagnostic measures .55 and .80 s thresholds with position-and-orientation or orientation alone before any preprocessing or training choice.

The paired 48-start stale-feature study r0212 was repeated across thresholds and components. At age .80 s, orientation-only masking retains 37 turns, raises ordered carry from 26 to 36 and keeps zero short-horizon travel faults and stops. It gives zero low upright entries, as baseline. Masking both stale pose components at .80 retains 37 turns and gives 35 carries, including 13 low upright entries, with three travel violations. reward_terms.name: lift

reward_terms.name: turn

reward_terms.name: carry
reward_terms.formula: Planar progress with weight 9 is multiplied by 0.25 + 0.75 times the measured height quality. Up to 6 points of causal height progress are added. body.text: The .80 s stale-pose feature intervention also shifts the separate r0217 trained network in a paired 48-start six-second check. Keeping the weights unchanged, masking both old invalid pose components changes ordered carry 24 to 30 and low held upright entries zero to three with 48 lifts and 36 turns in both. Neither seats upright in the first grip, no stops. The two arm J2 violations are both after separation, at 2.65 and 2.73 s with last contact 1.89 and 1.47 s. Evidence work/stale_pose080_r15_exact. This confirms a smaller effect than on r0208 and reinforces that the late commanded motion must be learned with the changed input. The candidate GPU and packaged NumPy feature transforms agree within 6.56e-7 on 180 exact observations, including ages around the threshold and valid poses. No policy kept from fixed-weight masking.

Through its 144.08M checkpoint, R15’s added height charge yielded lower early rise in some matched comparisons and no exact ordered placements. That checkpoint has 18 carries and three late arm travel violations, each after last plug contact. Inspecting the latest official gate failures r0161 shows grasp at .46 s then the unheld flat plug at 4.38 s in seeds 1024693583 and 1570065137. R16 will change only the actor’s handling of invalid retained pose features. At camera-reported age .80 s, use the empty-cache position and orientation features with the true validity and age, at training and deployment. This retains all turns and makes low held entries possible with fixed R14 and R15 weights (r0213/r0218), with faults after loss in the fixed-weight probes. This proposed PPO continuation tests whether the altered inputs can learn both lower transfer and safe post-loss behavior. It resumes the same original network and Adam state with -.100 middle MCP2, the same 388-state bank, sim4 physical strata, seed, the R15 reward and 26 min on four L40S. Preserve the exact station evaluator. Estimate both proximal and ordered support rates in 64 paired full starts. If it gives safety loss or no held support, compare the validated lower phase-3 reset bank as a later single change.

reward_terms.name: approach
reward_terms.formula: New maximum of approach potential from housing-to-palm position, wrist angle and two intended pads near the housing.

reward_terms.name: lift
reward_terms.formula: New clearance potential of a gripped object, gated by opposed contact and referenced to 14 mm.

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: New maximum of the minimum of world blade-up progress and signed tilt reduction attributable to relative angle changes; paid only while continuously opposed, unsupported, and the contact digits have measured and commanded motion. Common wrist rotation cancels in the relative measurement.

reward_terms.name: carry
reward_terms.formula: Planar progress with weight 9 is multiplied by 0.25 + 0.75 times the measured height quality. Up to 6 points of causal height progress are added. The height target interpolates the reconstructed transfer at the current lateral position, with 10 mm tolerance and 100 mm Gaussian scale. The upright plug remains held and unsupported through all controller ticks, the palm moves at least half as far as the object in the same vertical direction and its target changes in that direction. Only a new height-quality maximum pays. Each new height-quality minimum during an upright, held and unsupported transfer costs four times the decrease below the previous minimum. The level at entry is free.

reward_terms.name: seat
reward_terms.formula: New combined seating potential. Height score uses a 2 mm tolerance and 100 mm scale. Height credit requires an actual decrease in height error with downward movement at the palm of at least half of that distance, a descending target, blades within 25 degrees and contact preserved across controller ticks. Both policy samples are inside the goal. Tilt guidance keeps its existing scale. The potential starts at the measured entry value.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: New gain in removal of hand contact and supported upright rest.

reward_terms.name: reference_object
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in position and blade-axis agreement with the adapted reconstruction. Position and axis jointly use a 14 mm-equivalent tolerance.

reward_terms.name: reference_wrist
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in wrist position and orientation agreement with the adapted dense reconstruction. Airborne tolerance 83 mm and 0.70 rad, other phases 44 mm and 0.34 rad.

reward_terms.name: reference_posture
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in five-digit demonstrated flexion agreement with 0.53 rad RMS tolerance.

reward_terms.name: reference_contact
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in object-frame contact agreement with reconstructed witnesses within a 9 mm free band.

reward_terms.name: bonus
reward_terms.formula: One-time ordered approach, lift, turn, carry, seat and release bonuses 4, 6, 10, 12, 14 and 30. The training carry bonus and transition to seat require a held, controlled handoff within 35 mm of standing height.

reward_terms.name: slip
reward_terms.formula: Negative blade-angle displacement past 0.10 degree when an opposed grip moves the object with nearly stationary finger joints.

reward_terms.name: regularity
reward_terms.formula: Negative mean absolute target change, metres and radians.

reward_terms.name: stop
reward_terms.formula: Penalty at station stop or hardware violation.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Penalty on a dropped plug that settles unturned during the supported manipulation.

body.reflection: The scheduled 178.12M endpoint of the isolated height-deviation penalty scored 64 lifts, 36 turns, 16 ordered carries, zero ordered place/success, one violating episode, zero stops, five final rests and contract act p99 .252 ms. Seed 1030292 crossed the finger allowance at 14.42 s (max .02591 rad on index 7) and the arm J4 bound at 19.09 s (max 1.013 degrees from the IK limit), after ending plug contact at 6.13 s. R14 endpoint had 64/47/29 with no travel violations and one late stop. The conditional entry at R15 endpoint is still 125 mm above support, minimum while held 99 mm vs R14 116 mm, and median held time .725 vs .570 s. All 16 detach unsupported. The first .30 s from entry still raises the target by a median 50 mm. Earlier common-turn rises improved but there is no sustained ordered support or lower-stage gate candidate. No retained package. 94 updates on all four GPUs were 113,140 env steps/s inclusive and 115,256 after two updates. Median physics 7.117 s, controller 1.740 s, sensor .715 s, inference .141 s, resets 1.372 s, PPO 1.856 s including .375 s collectives. No capacity error and all 41 sampled complete contract audit traces pass. R16 isolates the input preprocessing under matched training settings, r0219.

body.text: The low fixed-weight mask cases r0221 have short clearance and braking headroom. Median object velocity at first low entry is +.207 m/s sideways and -.544 m/s vertically, with .110 s before first footprint exit. Ten of thirteen cross the positive-y edge and four cross the negative-x edge, with one combined exit. The r0141 controlled feasibility entries had about +.122 m/s sideways and -.010 m/s vertical median. The exact module and frozen gates are unchanged. If R16 learns low entries with the same drift, the next reward study can be targeted at conserving the upright hold near the goal and decelerating before support, using observed position and speed effects and a bounded one-time progress term. Evidence work/stale_pose080_low_entries_detail.json. This remains a hypothesis, independent of the active input-only study.

The r0200 early transfer with blade alignment tolerates a range of sideways entry speeds when the controlled fingers preserve the grip. On the same 24 exact verified-turn prefixes, fast/default/slow physical continuations have median entry y velocities .298/.223/.159 m/s and vertical velocities -.094/-.024/+.001 m/s. All 24 in each group retain contact through in-zone support with zero faults or stops. Upright first seats 15/14/14. Evidence work/low_transfer_pace_exact.json. The .207 m/s sideways median of r0223 is within this successful physical range, so a sideways speed ceiling alone is unsupported. The large vertical velocity, continued travel out of the target and late tilt remain better discriminators.

Over the first 100 ms after the 13 low masked-policy entries, the plug moves a median 6.32 mm and its blade axis rotates 16.35 degrees in the palm frame. The 13 low exact feasibility entries give 1.84 mm and 1.66 degrees in the same window, with eight first-grip support contacts. Masked median palm vertical speed over the preceding 40 ms is -.416 m/s alongside instantaneous plug speed -.544 m/s. The geometry and observed frame speeds support testing grip stabilization and controlled descent rather than a sideways velocity cap alone. Relative motion may include intentional adjustments, so this comparison does not by itself identify passive slip. Evidence work/low_entry_grip_relative_motion.json. No change to the active input-only run or exact evaluator.

body.reflection: At 35.51M active steps with both stale pose features masked at .80 s, exact64 gives 64 lifts, 42 active turns, 35 ordered carries, zero ordered places or successes, one arm travel violation, zero stops and 17 final rests. Act p99 .261 ms. Matched R15 C1 gives 64/45/28, no faults/stops and 13 rests. Across their 28 common verified turns, first .30 s rise is 66.7 vs 70.3 mm, peak 82.7 vs 133.9 mm and lateral displacement 132 vs 135 mm. Remaining continuous grasp .550 vs .945 s. R16 has ten same-grip upright entries within 35 mm of standing where R15 has zero. Conditional R16 entry/min still-held clearance 97/46 mm vs 119/110 and median target goes down 14 instead of up 51 mm early at entry. One exact carry, seed 911713, touches support while held at x=.44994 m (outside zone) and tilt 22.76 degrees, no qualifying seat. All other 34 detach before support. The separate J2 excursion seed 974123 starts at 2.73 s after contact ends at 1.91 s, max 1.148 degrees beyond the IK bound. No gate on this checkpoint. Continue until grip, orientation and safety effects are established.

body.text: The ten low held entries from the first trained masking checkpoint r0226 all leave the goal before support or separation. Eight first cross the negative-x edge and two the positive-y edge. Median time from low entry to exit is .030 s, minimum clearance still held inside is 22.5 mm, and entry vertical velocity is -.491 m/s. Over 100 ms the median grip-relative displacement is 4.13 mm and blade rotation 7.64 degrees, lower than the fixed-weight case at 6.32 mm and 16.35 degrees, still above the exact feasibility examples at 1.84 mm and 1.66 degrees. The one held support contact occurs outside x at 22.76 degrees tilt. Evidence work/r16_c1_low_entry_comparison.json. It identifies off-center landing as a problem even when the learned path produces substantial descent. No exact placement claim.

With the R16 learned mask in r0226, the 34 prepared low phase-3 suffixes give 19 low upright entries and three same-grip upright seats on cold observation reset. Restoring the actual stale observation cache gives 23 low entries and five seats, no stops in either case and two violations each. Zero terminal complete suffix in either mode. The same bank under r0208 with recorded cache had only one low entry and no held seat (r0209). The new observation processing now makes the low-transfer geometry useful under physically recorded sensor history. That distribution is a reasonable candidate for a later curriculum test. Evidence work/r16_c1_low_transfer_cold.json and work/r16_c1_low_transfer_recorded.json. Neither prepared rollout is a deployment score.

reward_terms.formula: New gain in removal of hand contact and supported upright rest.

reward_terms.name: reference_object
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in position and blade-axis agreement with the adapted reconstruction. Position and axis jointly use a 14 mm-equivalent tolerance.

reward_terms.name: reference_wrist
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in wrist position and orientation agreement with the adapted dense reconstruction. Airborne tolerance 83 mm and 0.70 rad, other phases 44 mm and 0.34 rad.

reward_terms.name: reference_posture
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in five-digit demonstrated flexion agreement with 0.53 rad RMS tolerance.

reward_terms.name: reference_contact
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in object-frame contact agreement with reconstructed witnesses within a 9 mm free band.

reward_terms.name: bonus
reward_terms.formula: One-time ordered approach, lift, turn, carry, seat and release bonuses 4, 6, 10, 12, 14 and 30. The training carry bonus and transition to seat require a held, controlled handoff within 35 mm of standing height.

reward_terms.name: slip
reward_terms.formula: Negative blade-angle displacement past 0.10 degree when an opposed grip moves the object with nearly stationary finger joints.

reward_terms.name: regularity
reward_terms.formula: Negative mean absolute target change, metres and radians.

reward_terms.name: stop
reward_terms.formula: Penalty at station stop or hardware violation.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Penalty on a dropped plug that settles unturned during the supported manipulation.

body.reflection: At 108.03M steps R16 has 64 lifts, 42 active turns, 38 ordered carries, zero ordered places/success, one late finger excursion, no stops, 13 rests and p99 .254 ms. R15 C3 matched 64/46/28 with one late fault. Across 28 common verified turns, peak rise 58.4 vs 124.7 mm, first .30 s rise 49.1 vs 63.6 mm and lateral displacement 132 mm both. There are 18 low in-grip upright entries against zero. Two in-zone first supports, including the first learned upright held support at seed 17623: 1.39 s, xyz .4884/.0570/-.29295 m, tilt 3.44 degrees, object linear .448 m/s and angular 9.58 rad/s. Holds after support, but lifts the plug off again at 1.40, exits by 1.53 and separates airborne at 1.95. The next .30 s commands go +109 mm y and +36 mm z. The montage shows the hand and plug lifting again then flat and separated at 4.02 s. No settled interval and final palm range 11 mm, final y .594 m. These are geometric support observations and zero complete placements. Conditional entry/min 84/49 mm and .225 s remaining hold. The separate fault seed 1030292 is a .02737 rad finger excursion at 10.49 s with last plug contact 1.89 s. Evidence work/r16_c3_first_supported_seat.json and work/r16_c3_first_support_montage.jpg. Continue R16 while the measured support behavior improves.

body.text: R16 C2 with -.100 middle MCP2 has no bare middle–ring overlap on all 64 nominal starts through 450 ms, minimum gap 1.719 mm. On a separate matched 16-start .1075 s/.010 rad test, enabling only the middle–ring pairs gives early max ring MCP2 excess .01479 rad and zero .02 rad travel excursions before 450 ms. Old geometry at the same delay/compliance gives .00915 rad max ring MCP2 excess and one early fault on another digit. The contact variant has 12/16 total violating episodes versus 8/16 without added pairs, gain five and remove one. Added-contact later faults include nine ring PIP excursions, first late faults mainly around 1.32–1.92 s. There are soft contacts during the ramp despite bare clearance. The early symptom is absent in this variant, with substantial post-grasp model sensitivity. Evidence work/finger_contact/r16_c2_contact_matched_delay_comparison.json and work/finger_contact/r16_c2_delayed_contact/hardware_faults.json. The exact evaluator and recorded sim4 remain intact. No claim of real target validation.
